candidates.original_title: Interpersonal predictors of group therapy outcome for complicated grief
candidates.description: Attachment insecurity predicts outcome following short-term group therapy for patients presenting with complicated grief, emerging as the strongest interpersonal predictor.
candidates.citation_sentence: In an analysis of data from a comparative trial of two forms (interpretive, supportive) of STG therapy (n = 107), Ogrodniczuk, Piper, McCallum, Joyce and Rosie reported that three distinct indices of interpersonal relatedness-quality of object relations, current social functioning and attachment insecurity-each had signifi cant relationships with measures of treatment outcome, with attachment insecurity emerging as the strongest predictor.
candidates.notes: The authors explicitly state that attachment insecurity emerged as a significant predictor of all three outcome factors when represented by the RSQ measures, providing a replication of the key finding. The RAQ overall score did not replicate the original result, but the broader attachment-security finding was supported.
